case_name: Kannusami v State of Tamil Nadu
respondent:
State of Tamil Nadu
Supreme Court of India

14 August 2001
Cr.A. No. 1284 of 1998; Cr.A. No. 77 of 1999
The Order of the Court was as follows:
1.  Three persons were convicted for the murder of the Vasu and all of them were sentenced to imprisonment for life for the offence under section 302 read with section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. The High Court on appeal filed by the three convicted persons confirmed the conviction and sentence and dismissed the appeal. They have come up before this Court by special leave.

statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code
By Resorting To Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The incident happened on 14.6.87 around 6.30 a.m. in the field of the father of deceased Vasu.
Vasu is the son of PW1 - Muniyandi Kohar, and his wife PW2 - Kolfamndi.
The said desertion was followed by the death of another son of A1.
Deceased Vasu went to the field for some agricultural operation during the morning hours, followed by his parents.
It was then that the three accused neared the deceased.
Thereafter A1 with a chopper and A2 with a knife inflicted cut injuries on Vasu.
He sustained large number of cut injuries many of them on the neck itself.
The information about the occurrence was conveyed by PW1 - Muniyandi to PW6 - who was the village administrative head from whom PW7 got the news.
An FIR was lodged by PW7 at 11.00 a.m. with the police station.
petitioner_arguments: One is that the clothes on the two parents were not smeared with even a stain of blood.
Second is that the information about the occurrence had reached the police station only several hours thereafter.
The possibility of the second accused being falsely implicated cannot be ruled out as PW1 and PW2 would have been nurturing vengeance towards the family of A1.
All that he did, according to the prosecution version, was to inflict a blow with a stick on the right shoulder.
court_reasoning: We cannot rule out the above possibility and therefore we cannot now say that the conduct of the parents was not natural.

The overall picture narrated above would indicate that there could not have been any possibility of PW1 deliberating himself or with others for the purpose of concocting a case against the three accused.
Unfortunately this aspect has not been utilised by the defence counsel in the trial court.

It was not done. Even no text book on 'Medical Jurisprudence' was cited before us to show that disappearance of rigour mortis on the hands would necessarily lead to an inference that death would have happened a couple of hours prior to 6.30 a.m.
Even that possibility is not enough for us to discard the testimony of PW1 and PW2 which was found reliable by the trial court and the High Court.
At any rate there is an area of doubt on that score.
We are inclined to extend the benefit of that doubt to A3.
holding: The appeal is disposed of accordingly. Appeal disposed of.
